label: D2 after choosing a1 and landing in S2 (rare transition a1->S2)
explanation: Fires only at D2, exactly when the last-action input is a1 and the shown state is S2, i.e. the rare transition after a1 (dev P=1.00, R=1.00). Never fires at D1/GO, never on a1->S1, a2->S2 or a2->S1. All variables are observed at D2. Magnitude is near-constant (median 4.6, max 5.2); it is modestly higher when the previous trial was unrewarded (prev_reward==0 covers 24% of the lowest vs 45% of the top activation quartile) and when S1 is the good state (77% vs 87% coverage across quartiles), i.e. when the rare outcome is more surprising/informative.

issues: No counterexamples found. On the test split the predicate scores P=R=F1=mass recall=1.0, with correlation 0.998 and 46977 active steps. misses --split test shows 0 missed activations and 0 false positives.
The predicate is the same as the version using the trial variables (phase==D2)&(action==1)&(state==2), which also scores 1.0 on test. Every term is observable at D2.

The feature is narrower than 'any rare transition at D2': (phase==D2)&(common==0) gives P=0.45 on test, so it does not fire on a2->S1. It is also narrower than 'S2 shown at D2': (phase==D2)&(in_state==2) gives P=0.23. This matches the claim that it fires only on a1->S2.

The magnitude claims hold on dev. prev_reward==0 covers 24% of the lowest activation quartile and 45% of the top. good==1 covers 77% of the lowest and 87% of the top. The 'more surprising' reading is interpretation, but it is minor and not a factual error.
